transcript: Last night, I saw a new play called Sulfur Bottom, about a small-town family embroiled in a constant struggle over whether to stay or go. Over the course of decades, we see how this family suffers from the very factories that had promised nothing but jobs and prospects. It's a piece about the impact of insidious policies on local communities and how we are to reckon with the concept of home as the world becomes increasingly uninhabitable. While I thought the show was at times disjointed or confusing, it was certainly thematically interesting, and it's nice to see new art taking on these conversations. The production is also partnering with Climate Week to raise awareness about environmental justice, and we had a brief talkback with some folks from We Act, a Harlem-based nonprofit working in the environmental justice space. Sulfur Bottom is running into mid-October and you can learn more about We Act at weact.org With that, another program for my collection.
